text:
Today on Earth, Vice President JD Vance said Iran must meaningfully reduce nuclear enrichment before the seven-month war can end. He said Washington is speaking with Iran’s president and foreign minister but remains unsure who holds final authority. President Trump said nobody knows who is running Iran.

Saudi authorities said Houthi attacks on the airports in Jazan and Najran injured three people. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces also advanced around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait after retaking territory from the Iran-backed rebels.

Ukraine launched one of the war’s largest drone attacks against Moscow and its surrounding region. Moscow’s mayor said more than 650 drones targeted the capital. Regional officials reported two deaths, seven injuries and damage to dozens of homes. Russian bloggers said a major fuel depot was struck, but authorities had not confirmed it.

More than 250,000 students, teachers and parents marched across France over school funding, staff shortages and deteriorating facilities. Police used tear gas and water cannons, and 488 people were arrested.

The protest over French school funding came complete with Palestinian flags. Every cause now arrives with the same accessories.

The U.S. military suspended operations in Okinawa for 48 hours and restricted troops from leaving their bases after a Marine was arrested on suspicion of killing a local woman and stealing her belongings.

Satellite images reviewed by Reuters showed eight light attack aircraft and more than two dozen military vehicles at a new China-Laos facility. Analysts said the expanding airfield could become China’s first fully operational military base in Southeast Asia.

Colombia’s president offered legal assistance to 17 Colombian veterans extradited from Haiti to Florida over their alleged involvement in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. He also promised support for their families.

Tropical Depression Nine formed in the Gulf of Mexico and was forecast to become the Atlantic season’s first hurricane before approaching Louisiana and Mississippi. Its path crosses offshore fields responsible for 15% of U.S. oil production.

The World Bank raised its 2026 growth forecast for Sub-Saharan Africa to 4.3% but warned that living standards were not rising as quickly and roughly half the region’s countries were either in default or struggling with debt.

The Justice Department instructed employees to use “super intelligence” instead of “artificial intelligence” in most official contexts, including court proceedings.

The intelligence remains artificial. The terminology is now mandatory.

Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics for pioneering the detection of high-energy neutrinos known as ghost particles. His IceCube Observatory uses more than 5,000 sensors buried in Antarctic ice to detect particles from distant galaxies.

Paramount Skydance completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, placing CBS, CNN, HBO Max, Paramount+, Warner Bros. and DC Studios under one company carrying approximately $80 billion in debt.

Hollywood consolidated the competition. The subscriptions remain separate for now.

The death of televangelist Jim Bakker was reported today. He died Monday at 86 after building a multimillion-dollar Christian television empire that collapsed amid sex and financial scandals, a fraud conviction and imprisonment.

On this day in 1927, The Jazz Singer premiered in New York. Its synchronized music and dialogue helped launch talking motion pictures and accelerate the end of silent cinema.

That was one day on Earth.

See you tomorrow. Same planet. The ghost particles are elusive. The headlines are not. 🌎

In February, Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother and half-brother at their family home before fatally shooting five students and an education assistant at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School. She later killed herself.

The lengthy indictment against Bryant sheds new light on Van Rootselaar’s apparent actions and state of mind, and alleges for the first time that another person helped plan the shooting.

text:
▫️🏠 High Mortgage Rates Are Now Squeezing Home Sellers, Too▫️

📉 Sellers are losing leverage: The U.S. housing slowdown is increasingly hitting homeowners trying to sell. With mortgage rates back above 7%, fewer buyers can afford current prices, forcing sellers to compete harder for a much smaller pool of qualified purchasers. 

✂️ Price cuts are surging: In September, 20.8% of U.S. listings had a price reduction, the highest September share since 2018. Price cuts were particularly widespread in the West, where 22.8% of listings were reduced. 

🏘️ Inventory is piling up: There were roughly 1.16 million active listings in September, up 5.4% from a year earlier. At the same time, homes going under contract have weakened, creating a widening gap between supply and actual buyer demand. 

💰 Even discounts aren't solving affordability: Sellers can cut $10,000 or $20,000 from an asking price, but higher borrowing costs can overwhelm those savings. A 30-year mortgage was averaging around 7.3%–7.6% in early October, dramatically increasing monthly payments compared with rates earlier this year. 

⏳ Sellers face an unpleasant choice: Owners who don't urgently need to move can withdraw their properties and wait. But people dealing with relocations, divorces, financial pressure or already-purchased replacement homes may have little choice but to cut prices, offer concessions or help buyers buy down their mortgage rates. 

🔑 The housing market's imbalance is changing: This isn't necessarily a nationwide housing crash. Instead, the market is shifting from the extreme seller advantage of previous years toward buyers—while simultaneously remaining extremely difficult for buyers because financing is so expensive. That unusual combination means buyers have more negotiating power but less purchasing power, while sellers have valuable homes but fewer people capable of buying them. 

📊 Bottom line: America's housing freeze is increasingly becoming a seller problem as well as a buyer problem. Unless mortgage rates fall substantially, home prices adjust further, or incomes catch up, transactions can remain depressed even while the number of homes available for sale keeps rising.

text:
Would you want to play in Boston or Tampa if you were an athlete @TonyMassarotti 

Key Financial Differences

1. The Home Game "Millionaire Tax" Penalty
A Red Sox player pays a steep marginal tax rate of 9% on roughly half of their entire salary (the 81 home games plus local training days). Conversely, a Rays player pays 0% state tax on all 81 home games. [1, 2]
•Example: On a $10,000,000 salary, assuming roughly half of the athlete's duty days are logged at home, a Red Sox player will forfeit roughly $450,000directly to the state of Massachusetts just for their home games. A Rays player keeps 100% of that portion.

2. Spring Training Allocation
An MLB season begins in mid-February with Spring Training. Both the Red Sox (Fort Myers) and the Rays train in Florida. However, because the Red Sox are a Massachusetts-based entity, those early duty days can still be factored into the player's primary residency allocation or W-2 pool depending on the player's legal domicile. For the Rays, those 45+ days of spring training are strictly logged in a 0% tax state. [1, 2, 3]

3. Divisional Jock Tax Exposure
Because both teams play in the AL East, they share a similar travel schedule. However, their total net exposure differs: [1]
•The Rays' Net Savings: Even when traveling to play the Red Sox at Fenway Park or the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, the Rays player only pays the high "jock taxes" for those specific 3-to-4 day road series. The rest of their year remains untaxed at the state level. [1, 2, 3]
•The Red Sox Double-Whammy: A Red Sox player gets hit by the 9% tax at home, and still has to pay the local jock taxes when traveling to New York, Toronto, California, or Baltimore. [1, 2]

The Bottom Line
If a free agent is offered an identical $20 million per year contract by both teams, the player signing with the Tampa Bay Rays will net roughly $700,000 to $900,000 more per year in take-home pay purely due to state tax differences.

text:
Crypto card transaction volume reaches $12.5B amid stablecoin payment growth

Crypto card payment volume has reached a reported record of $12.5 billion, according to data from https://t.co/YQILadgdiJ cited by The Kobeissi Letter. The figure represents a 140% increase since the start of the year and is 247% above the level recorded in October 2025. The reported growth is linked to increasing use of stablecoins for everyday transactions and cross-border payments, where digital assets can potentially offer faster settlement and lower costs than traditional rails.

QR-code spending is also contributing to usage. Activated cards on Jupiter Spend, described as a major on-chain card provider, rose 55% quarter over quarter, although the report does not provide absolute card numbers or detailed methodology for the broader market estimate.

Several companies are expanding their crypto-card offerings. Fold Holdings has begun issuing its Bitcoin Credit Card to selected waitlist users through Visa and Stripe Issuing. The product offers bitcoin rewards, with the standard rate listed at 1.5% and higher rates available through promotions and user activity. Aven’s Bitcoin Visa Card instead allows customers to borrow against bitcoin collateral without selling it. The card has reported rates beginning at 7.99% APR, with BitGo providing custody and Coastal Community Bank acting as issuer. The figures indicate growing payment experimentation, but do not establish that crypto cards have achieved mass-market adoption.

🛏️ If You Want to Change the World, Start by Making Your Bed.

In 2014, Naval Admiral William H. McRaven stood before the graduating class at the University of Texas at Austin.

 As the commander of U.S. Special Operations Command—the man who oversaw the raid that captured Osama bin Laden—people expected an address filled with grand military strategy.

Instead, he gave them a piece of advice so simple it caught the world by surprise: "If you want to change the world, start off by making your bed."

The wisdom behind this simple, daily habit contains a masterclass in human psychology, discipline, and building massive victories from tiny tasks.

🧠 The Psychology of the First Completed Task
During basic Navy SEAL training, students are required to make their beds to absolute perfection every single morning. At the time, it felt ridiculous to aspiring, battle-hardened warriors. But McRaven explained the deep underlying purpose:

Making your bed provides an immediate, completed task that sets a psychological precedent for productivity and momentum throughout the day. You can find the full quote regarding this first daily task in the referenced web document.

⚖️ Why the Little Things Matter
McRaven’s address highlights that macro excellence is built on micro discipline. Handling small responsibilities correctly builds the foundation required for high-stakes achievements.
The full explanation of why mastering small details is essential for bigger accomplishments can be found in the referenced web document.

🛡️ Building a Sanctuary Against Failure
A neatly made bed serves as a psychological anchor when facing a difficult or chaotic day. Returning to a controlled environment offers quiet encouragement that tomorrow brings a fresh start. The full details regarding this comfort are available in the referenced web document.

📈 The 10 Lessons to Change the World
McRaven outlined 10 universal rules derived from Navy SEAL training to help navigate life's challenges:

Start the day with a task completed. (Make your bed)

Find someone to help you paddle. (You can't change the world alone)

Measure a person by the size of their heart. (Respect everyone)

Get over being a sugar cookie and keep moving forward. (Accept that life isn't fair and setbacks happen)

Don't be afraid of the circuses. (Embrace challenges and failures)

Sometimes you have to slide down the obstacle head-first. (Take calculated risks)

Don't back down from the sharks. (Confront bullies and face your fears)

Be your very best in the darkest moments. (Step up when stakes are high)

Start singing when you're up to your neck in mud. (Deliver hope and positivity)

Never, ever ring the bell. (Never give up on your goals)

💡 The Big Takeaway
Big success stems from consistent execution of small, daily actions. To transform your path, begin with the fundamentals. 
Go make your bed.

text:
$MRVL surged 6.7% after lifting its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20B and laying out a $70B-$90B fiscal 2031 target, while $AMD gained 3.8% as Lisa Su said supply will rise substantially in 2027. 

$CEG jumped about 13% after Google signed a 3,590 MW power deal, and $OPCH soared 32.9% on a $5.8B take-private by McKesson and CD&R. 

Everything that mattered in the market today:

https://t.co/hWRPIyS19w DAILY ROUNDUP - OCTOBER 6, 2026

👉 COMPANIES

1. $MRVL: closed at $289.32, up 6.7%, after raising its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20B from $18B. Management also projected $70B-$90B of fiscal 2031 revenue, far above current Street expectations, as custom AI silicon and interconnect demand accelerates.

2. $AMD: closed around $655, up about 3.8%, after CEO Lisa Su said AMD plans to substantially increase chip supply in 2027 to meet booming AI demand. 

3. $AVGO: closed at $377.78, up 4.2%, as Marvell’s aggressive custom-silicon forecasts reinforced the scale of hyperscaler demand for non-Nvidia AI accelerators. 

4. $CEG: closed near $303, up about 13%, after Google agreed to a 3,590 MW power package. The deal includes a 20-year agreement enabling 890 MW of incremental nuclear output and more than $4.3B of investment across Constellation reactors. 

5. $VST: closed around $159, up roughly 10%, as nuclear generators rerated after Google’s Constellation deal and federal support for up to $4.2B of Vistra nuclear upgrades. 

6. $NRG: gained about 7.4% as investors extended the AI-power trade beyond nuclear operators to merchant generators with exposure to tightening U.S. power markets. 

7. $CIEN: surged roughly 11.5% as Marvell’s investor-day forecasts strengthened the case for a multiyear optical-networking and AI interconnect spending cycle. 

8. $FIX: gained about 6% as investors continued to price strong data-center construction demand into electrical and mechanical infrastructure contractors. 

9. $ANET: rose about 3.5% as the AI networking complex benefited from stronger long-term forecasts for switching and interconnect demand. 

10. $NBIS: gained about 8.7%, extending volatility in AI infrastructure names as investors continued to reward companies with scarce compute capacity. 

11. $NVDA: closed at $239.88, up 0.4%. The broader AI complex rallied, but Marvell’s custom-silicon targets highlighted the growing hyperscaler effort to diversify accelerator architectures. 

12. $SPCX: closed at $171.69, up about 0.4%, while fresh analyst attention focused on Starlink’s subscriber growth and SpaceX’s expanding communications infrastructure footprint.

13. $STX: fell about 9.6% to $802.02 as investors took profits in storage names after a powerful AI-memory and storage rally. 

14. $WDC: fell about 7.6% to $408.30 alongside Seagate as the storage trade reversed sharply despite continued long-term AI data-growth optimism. 

15. $MRNA: fell about 6.2% to roughly $190 as investors continued to reassess valuation after its extraordinary 2026 rally and recent bearish analyst calls. 

👉 EARNINGS

16. $LW: jumped about 7% after fiscal Q1 adjusted EPS of $0.75 beat expectations near $0.59 and revenue reached $1.67B. Lamb Weston raised fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.05-$3.35 from $2.95-$3.25. 

17. $STZ: reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $2.63B, up 6%, and comparable EPS of $3.74 versus roughly $3.55 expected. Beer sales rose 5%, wine and spirits 17%, and full-year earnings guidance was raised. 

18. $APOG: rallied after quarterly sales of $391.1M topped expectations and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.00-$3.40 from $2.70-$3.25. 

👉 ANALYST ACTIONS

19. $CTVA: jumped roughly 13% after JPMorgan upgraded the post-spin crop-protection company to Buy and set a $19 target, arguing the standalone business trades at a depressed valuation after the Vylor separation. 

20. $CLF: was upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight at Wells Fargo, which called Cleveland-Cliffs its preferred tactical steel idea heading into Q3 earnings.

21. $SHOP: remained Overweight at JPMorgan as the firm raised its price target to $200.

👉 M&A / CAPITAL MOVES

22. $OPCH: closed around $31.06, up 32.9%, after McKesson and CD&R agreed to acquire Option Care Health for $32.05 per share in a transaction valued at about $5.8B including debt. The offer represents roughly a 37% premium to the prior close. 

23. $MCK: will invest about $1.4B for a 49% stake in Option Care Health, while CD&R will own 51%. The structure gives McKesson a framework to acquire CD&R’s interest later. 

24. $UBER: agreed to acquire workplace-catering platform ezCater for $2.3B in cash. ezCater generated more than $2.5B of trailing-12-month gross bookings, grew in the high teens and has average orders above $400. 

25. $ET: agreed to acquire Vaquero Midstream for about $2.625B in cash and stock, expanding natural-gas processing and pipeline capacity in the Delaware Basin.

26. $SKYD: completed the roughly $110B Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery combination and began trading on the NYSE under the SKYD ticker. The combined company targets at least 30 films annually and roughly $6B of cost reductions. 

👉 MANAGEMENT / WORKFORCE

27. $HUBS: announced a restructuring that will eliminate about 660 jobs, or 7% of its workforce. HubSpot expects $65M-$75M of charges and said the reorganization is intended to align the company around an AI-first operating model rather than simply reduce costs. 

👉 PRODUCT / PARTNERSHIPS

28. $GOOGL: signed one of the largest U.S. corporate power arrangements yet with Constellation: 3,590 MW in PJM, including 890 MW of new nuclear capacity under a 20-year agreement and another 2,700 MW under a 15-year deal.

👉 MARKET THEMES

29. U.S. INDEXES: the S&P 500 gained about 0.6% to 7,820.47, the Nasdaq rose about 0.5% to 27,604.74, and the Dow advanced roughly 0.5% to 51,531.57. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished at record closing highs. 

30. TREASURIES: the 10-year Treasury yield eased to roughly 5.27% from 5.31% Monday, giving growth equities some relief while remaining near multidecade highs. 

31. OIL: crude stabilized after recent declines, easing some inflation anxiety that had driven bond yields higher. Energy prices remain a key input into Fed expectations. 

32. U.S. TRADE: the August trade deficit widened 13.7% to roughly $105.6B as imports reached a record. Capital-goods imports rose 4.4%, with AI infrastructure contributing to demand for semiconductors, computers and related equipment. 

33. AI CAPEX: the EIA now expects U.S. electricity consumption to reach records of about 4,288 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,356 billion kWh in 2027, with AI and crypto data centers among the major demand drivers. 

34. SOFTWARE: the S&P 500 software and services index reached fresh 2026 highs as earnings expectations improved. Expected 2026 earnings growth for the group has risen to about 20.6% from 13.8% in March. 

35. EARNINGS SEASON: LSEG estimates S&P 500 Q3 earnings will rise about 30.6% year over year, including roughly 66.5% growth for technology and 114.7% for energy. 

36. FED: markets continued to price a lower probability of another October rate hike as oil stabilized and yields retreated; Wednesday’s Fed minutes are the next major policy catalyst. 

👉 STOCKS TO WATCH

37. $MRVL: the new $20B fiscal 2028 target and $70B-$90B fiscal 2031 range dramatically raise the bar. Investors now need customer ramps and gross-margin execution to validate forecasts that extend well beyond current consensus. 

38. $CEG: the Google agreement puts an explicit value on incremental nuclear capacity. Watch whether similar hyperscaler contracts spread across the sector and whether Constellation can execute $4.3B+ of upgrades on schedule. 

39. $VST: federal financing plus hyperscaler nuclear contracts are changing the economics of existing reactors. The next question is how much of that scarcity value flows into long-term contracted power prices.

40. $OPCH: with shares near the $32.05 offer, the remaining spread should primarily reflect regulatory approval, shareholder approval and time to the expected first-half-2027 close. 

41. $AMD: the 2027 supply expansion is bullish only if demand remains ahead of capacity. Watch accelerator shipments, hyperscaler wins and gross margins as AMD scales against Nvidia and custom silicon. 

42. $STX / $WDC: Tuesday’s sharp reversal is a reminder that supply-tightness trades can become crowded. Watch contract pricing, inventory and capacity additions rather than extrapolating spot shortages indefinitely.

43. $HUBS: the 7% workforce reduction creates a clean test of AI-era software economics: can HubSpot accelerate product output and customer outcomes without weakening growth or sales execution? 

44. $UBER: ezCater adds a higher-ticket corporate order stream to delivery. Watch whether $400+ average catering orders improve unit economics enough to justify the $2.3B cash purchase. 

👉 DEEP ANALYSIS / MARKET INTELLIGENCE

45. CUSTOM SILICON IS BECOMING A SECOND AI COMPUTE MARKET: MRVL’s fiscal 2031 revenue midpoint of $80B is roughly 71% above the $46.85B Visible Alpha consensus cited around its investor day, while AVGO rose 4.2% in sympathy. This is not simply another semiconductor rally: hyperscalers are increasingly willing to fund proprietary accelerators and networking silicon to reduce dependence on a single GPU architecture. NVDA can keep growing while its share of incremental AI silicon dollars becomes less dominant.

46. POWER SCARCITY IS MOVING FROM NARRATIVE TO CONTRACT: Google’s 3,590 MW agreement with CEG includes 890 MW of incremental nuclear capacity and enables more than $4.3B of investment. At the same time, VST is tied to up to $4.2B of federal financing for nuclear upgrades. The second-order effect is important: AI infrastructure is beginning to create long-duration contracted cash flows for generation assets that were once valued largely as commodity power exposure. 

47. THE AI CAPITAL CYCLE IS NOW VISIBLE IN U.S. TRADE DATA: U.S. capital-goods imports rose 4.4% in August while the overall trade deficit widened to about $105.6B. Separate EIA forecasts put U.S. power demand at record levels in both 2026 and 2027. Chips, servers, networking, cooling and electricity are no longer separate AI themes; they are one physical capital cycle, and the bottleneck is moving progressively downstream from GPUs toward interconnect and power. 

48. OPTION CARE SHOWS WHY HOME-BASED HEALTHCARE ATTRACTS STRATEGIC CAPITAL: OPCH received a $5.8B enterprise-value offer at a 37% premium, with MCK committing $1.4B for 49%. Option Care serves more than 300,000 patients annually and moves complex infusion therapy away from higher-cost hospital settings. McKesson is effectively buying exposure to the site-of-care shift while preserving a path to full control later. 

49. SOFTWARE’S AI DISRUPTION TRADE IS REVERSING: the S&P 500 software and services index reached fresh 2026 highs while expected sector earnings growth rose to 20.6% from 13.8% in March. That matters because the first AI valuation shock assumed agents would destroy SaaS pricing power. Current results from large software vendors suggest a different near-term outcome: incumbents with distribution, proprietary workflow data and customer relationships can monetize AI before replacement risk becomes material. 

50. STORAGE’S REVERSAL IS A CAPITAL-CYCLE WARNING: STX fell about 9.6% and WDC about 7.6% after huge AI-driven runs. Storage fundamentals may still be strong, but supply-constrained industries often produce their best earnings just as investors begin capitalizing peak pricing too far into the future. The next decisive variables are capacity additions, contract pricing and whether AI data growth absorbs new supply faster than producers bring it online. 

51. HIGHER RATES HAVE NOT BROKEN AI EQUITIES—BUT THEY RAISE THE QUALITY BAR: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached records while the 10-year yield remained around 5.27%. A 5%+ risk-free rate makes distant cash flows expensive, yet MRVL, AMD, CEG and networking names rallied because investors are seeing concrete revenue, contracts and capacity demand. The market is increasingly separating AI stories backed by contracted economics from those relying mainly on future narratives.

text:
I wrote Rocky, but they offered me $360,000 NOT to be in it...Sylvester Stallone shares the wildest stories from his life of hard graft and grit
dailymail.com3 days ago

Sylvester Stallone lasted only three and a half weeks as a lion cage cleaner. It wasn’t so much that the cleaning itself was difficult but that the powerful ammoniac stench of the lions’ urine made his eyes stream. Added to that, the reek clung to his clothes ‘as if I had the world’s greatest bladder problem’. He was also unnerved by the lions balefully gazing at him through the bars of the neighbouring cage. ‘The way they inhaled and exhaled made an eerie moaning sound like they already knew what I was going to taste like,’ he writes.

The Steps, the 80-year-old star’s first memoir, is his account of his life from 1969, when he returned to the US after backpacking around Europe and literally walked into the lion’s den in Central Park Zoo, to 1976, when Rocky, the story about a boxer that he wrote and starred in, was released and became a blockbuster hit. We also get some illuminating flashbacks about his family life.

I had no idea what to expect from this but it’s an absolute knockout; a hugely entertaining page-turner that is both funny and uplifting. Stallone, desperate to break into showbusiness, faces setback after setback. Agents, directors and producers are rude about the way he looks, the way he sounds and his acting ability. It all hurts. Stallone, despite his tough-guy build and demeanour, is a deeply sensitive soul with a head full of poetry. Yet, after every knockback, insult or slight, he simply picks himself up, gives himself a pep talk and carries on. He just won’t stay down. When he finally does get some breaks, I cheered for him.

He was born in July 1946 and the forceps used to deliver him crushed a nerve, paralysing the left side of his face, and leaving him with a crooked mouth and a slur. His family live in a grotty apartment in Hell’s Kitchen, New York City. Both parents are given to volcanic rages and always fighting. He craves their love but has a difficult relationship with both, particularly his mother. ‘She constantly reminded me that the only reason I was even alive was that the coat hanger didn’t work and neither did her bouncing down the stairs,’ he recalls.

Despite this, or maybe because of it, Stallone grows up to be resilient and determined. After his European jaunt, he rents a tiny room in a dodgy New York hotel. Virtually penniless, he showers in his clothes to wash them at the same time as himself. He lives off two tablespoons of cottage cheese and four raw eggs a day. He wants to be an actor, he studied drama at the University of Miami (he didn’t finish his degree), so when he’s not working in one of a series of dead-end jobs, he’s lucklessly trawling around the city’s talent agents.

He attends an open audition but doesn’t realise it’s for a musical. Asked to sing a song, he attempts the only number he knows by heart, a weird psychedelic epic rock song by Procol Harum, In Held ‘Twas In I. He doesn’t get the role. That’s fine, he writes, because ‘I needed to practise for failure … Rejection is your shadow at every step in this business.’

Eventually, things start slowly picking up. He gets a job as a cinema usher and records the films on a tape recorder. After his shift, he writes up all the dialogue, analysing why an audience laughs here or cries there. An aspiring actress called Sasha starts working at the cinema and she and Stallone hit it off.

text:
🧠 The announcement of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honors a turning point in humanity's quest to understand the brain. 

By awarding Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel, and Karl Deisseroth, the Nobel Assembly recognized optogenetics—a breakthrough technology that enables researchers to manipulate living neural circuits using light.

For generations, deciphering the central nervous system stood as biology’s most formidable frontier. Housing over eighty billion neurons exchanging brief electrical impulses across trillions of synapses, the brain operates at a millisecond cadence that conventional laboratory tools struggled to disentangle with precision.

Historically, neuroscientists relied on techniques that faced difficult trade-offs. While electrical microstimulation could establish causal links by activating neural tissue, metal electrodes stimulated cells without genetic discrimination, recruiting mixed populations of different neuronal types and passing axons alike.

Brain imaging tools like functional magnetic resonance imaging offered a panoramic view across anatomical regions, but they only tracked the delayed blood-oxygen response occurring seconds after neural activity had passed. Science could observe which areas correlated with behaviors, but lacked tools to rapidly isolate specific cell types.

The resolution to this dilemma emerged from an unexpected biological curiosity: pond scum. In the early 2000s, German biophysicist Peter Hegemann investigated how the single-celled green alga *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* senses light to orient its swimming toward favorable light conditions.

Human vision relies on complex cascades where photoreceptors require multiple enzymes to translate incoming light into an electrical signal. In contrast, Hegemann and his collaborators identified that algal phototaxis relied on channelrhodopsins—proteins that integrated both light sensing and ion transport within a single molecular structure.

Collaborating with Hegemann and Ernst Bamberg, biophysicist Georg Nagel expressed these algal proteins in frog egg cells to measure their electrical properties. He demonstrated that channelrhodopsin-2 functioned as a light-gated cation channel, opening a central pore that allowed positive ions to rush inward when illuminated by blue light.

Nagel and Hegemann confirmed that this light-gated mechanism was functional in the animal cells tested. When the genetic sequence encoding channelrhodopsin-2 was introduced into foreign host cells, the cells produced the protein and embedded it directly into their surface membranes, creating an operable molecular switch.

At Stanford University, neuroscientist and psychiatrist Karl Deisseroth was motivated by the clinical difficulty of treating psychiatric conditions to seek better tools for mapping neural circuits. Partnering with graduate researchers Edward Boyden and Feng Zhang, Deisseroth set out to introduce channelrhodopsin-2 into mammalian nerve cells.

In optogenetics, researchers use DNA control sequences known as promoters to help direct gene expression to selected cell types. Packaged into engineered viral vectors—microscopic biological vehicles repurposed for gene delivery—the genetic instructions prompt target neurons to manufacture the algal protein and embed it into their membranes.

In their landmark 2005 study, co-authored with Nagel and Bamberg, the team tested this approach in cultured rodent neurons. When pulsed with blue light, the light-gated channels opened, positive ions surged inward, and the neurons fired action potentials—the cell's native electrical impulses—with crisp millisecond temporal precision.

By 2007, researchers including Deisseroth and Luis de Lecea achieved selective optical control inside living, behaving mammals. Delivering blue light via optical fibers, they targeted hypocretin neurons—specialized cells associated with wakefulness—in the hypothalamus, demonstrating that optical stimulation significantly increased the probability of waking sleeping mice and confirming a direct causal role in arousal.

The optogenetic toolkit soon expanded beyond excitation to include cellular inhibition. Researchers introduced halorhodopsin, which pumps chloride ions inward under yellow light, and archaerhodopsin, which pumps protons outward, allowing scientists to rapidly suppress action potentials and test what happens when specific circuits fall silent.

This breakthrough takes on fresh relevance as modern brain-computer interfaces, most visibly Elon Musk’s Neuralink, capture public imagination. While optogenetics and commercial interfaces both aim to decipher neural communication, they address related challenges through fundamentally different engineering philosophies.

Neuralink’s N1 implant pursues a bioelectronic approach, distributing 1,024 electrodes across 64 flexible polymer threads. The device focuses on reading neural activity, training mathematical decoders on recorded spikes to translate a patient’s motor intentions into digital cursor commands on a computer screen.

However, bioelectronic devices encounter distinct physical constraints when attempting to write information back into neural tissue. Passing current through extracellular fluid produces distributed electrical fields that can recruit mixed populations of neurons and passing axons, whereas optogenetics uses genetic promoters to target optical sensitivity to defined cell populations.

Yet achieving cellular precision solves only half the puzzle. Controlling which neurons fire and knowing which complex spatial and temporal firing patterns will produce a coherent, useful perception or behavior remain entirely separate scientific challenges that both optical and electronic systems must ultimately confront.

These two approaches represent complementary disciplines rather than competing substitutes. Optogenetics provides the experimental tools to test the causal functions of distinct cell types, while electrical interfaces develop the real-time decoders necessary to translate collective neural firing into assistive prosthetic control.

Translational tradeoffs explain why electrode arrays remain the primary approach for clinical neuroprosthetics in human motor cortex. While electrode insertion requires delicate neurosurgery, brain-directed optogenetics requires viral gene delivery to modify human neurons alongside light delivery through opaque tissue that heavily scatters photons.

Where optogenetics has crossed into human clinical trials is in the eye, where natural optical transparency overcomes the light-delivery bottleneck. In conditions like retinitis pigmentosa, light-sensing photoreceptors degenerate, but downstream retinal neurons can survive and be genetically engineered into functional light sensors.

In a landmark 2021 clinical report, a patient with advanced retinitis pigmentosa received a viral vector carrying the gene for the amber-light-activated opsin ChrimsonR, targeting the retina's output neurons, known as retinal ganglion cells. Paired with specialized light-projecting goggles, the patient recovered partial functional vision, successfully locating, counting, and touching objects on a table.

This outcome provides a telling contrast with Neuralink’s Blindsight initiative. While Blindsight pursues the ambitious goal of restoring visual perception by stimulating the visual cortex farther downstream in the brain, optogenetic therapies utilize surviving ocular circuitry to process and relay signals through natural visual pathways.

Ultimately, the 2026 Nobel Prize honors the profound and unpredictable reach of curiosity-driven science. A journey that began with basic questions about how single-celled algae navigate toward sunlight has yielded an indispensable light switch for neural circuits, reshaping our fundamental understanding of the living brain.

The Church told French Canadians that money, business, industry, and cities were dirty, and that they should return to the land, find God, and farm potatoes. When that trad reactionary social order failed to deliver either prosperity or political victory over the “White Anglo Saxon Protestants,” who were mostly Anglo Québécois of Scottish and Irish ancestry mixed with French Canadian heritage, communists were there to exploit the failure.

They chimped out and slurped up Third Worldist rhetoric from Marxist Leninists like Pierre Vallières and Charles Gagnon, who recast the consequences of Quebec’s own clerical, ruralist, and educational order as the product of colonial oppression. They embraced the lies of Michèle Lalonde, who propagated the myth that French Canadians were told to “speak white.”

There was no formal law or legal discrimination against French Canadians in Quebec in any capacity. But Third Worldism, much like Irish nationalism, became powerful because it offered an explanation. 

Instead of examining the failures of the institutions that had governed French Canadian society for centuries, they blamed an external Anglo oppressor, who were ironically not English, usually Catholic, and part French by blood. 

The irony is that the French Canadian middle class throughout the 19th and early 20th centuries built immense enterprises, department stores, legal firms, industries, steamship companies, credit unions, and financial institutions in Montreal. French Canadians also worked extensively for the major banks, chiefly RBC and BMO, both of which remain legally headquartered in Montreal today and are officially Quebec corporations.

MMAT ⚖️🦋
In re Meta Materials Inc.
U.S. Bankruptcy Court — District of Nevada
Case No. 24-50792-gs
DOCS. 3002 & 3003 + EXHIBITS 3003-1 THROUGH 3003-4
Filed October 6, 2026

⚠️ NOT LEGAL ADVICE - LONG ONE!

📄⚖️ TODAY’S FILINGS

DOC. 3002: Trustee Christina Lovato’s response to objections to selling the Authentix & 24M litigation claims.

DOC. 3003: Attorney Jeffrey Hartman’s sworn declaration, with historical emails, Meta’s 2024 McCabe settlement & the 2026 tolling agreement.

These support the sale—not a ruling approving it.

💰🦋 THE DEAL

BaileyBridge, wholly owned & controlled by McCabe, buys the claims. The estate receives:

💵 $250,000.
📈 20% of NET recoveries.
🏦 BaileyBridge funds future litigation.

The trustee says this provides cash & potential upside without estate funding.

📣 “Demand figures in complaints are not a valuation.”

Meaning: requesting millions does not establish a lawsuit’s sale value.

🏛️🛑 RESPONSE TO AUTHENTIX

The trustee argues Authentix lacks standing to block the sale: it is neither a creditor nor a shareholder. Changing who pursues the lawsuit does not change its defenses or liability.

📣 “Its remedy is to defend the adversary proceeding.”

Authentix also wants to bid. The trustee identifies the hearing as an opportunity for better offers.

🔐⚖️ McCABE CLAIMS REMAIN SEPARATE

The trustee says she retains potential claims against McCabe rather than selling them.

Regarding tolling:

📣 “It does not release Mr. McCabe.”

Hartman states under penalty of perjury:

📣 “At no time during the events leading up to the execution of the Tolling Agreement, was there any discussion about McCabe acquiring the rights to pursue claims against Authentix.”

His point: tolling & the sale were separate arrangements.

📅🔍 TOLLING AGREEMENT — ATTACHED VIA DROPBOX

It pauses applicable deadlines for covered claims for one year from JULY 17, 2026, subject to extension or earlier termination. It does not revive expired claims or establish liability.

📝 Doc. 3002 references July 7; Hartman & the agreement identify JULY 17.

📨🔎 THE EMAILS

EXHIBIT 1 contains McCabe’s questions about whether Meta’s board discussed removing Palikaras, a reverse split or bankruptcy BEFORE approving his stock-purchase agreement.

📣 “Is there a credible pathway for Meta to stay viable as a company?”

Hartman says it is unknown whether Meta responded. Questions are not proof of concealment.

EXHIBIT 2 records proposed settlement terms.

📜⚖️ THE SEPARATE 2024 RELEASE

EXHIBIT 3: Settlement effective JANUARY 22, 2024, before bankruptcy. It ended McCabe’s remaining stock-purchase obligations & required:

💵 $700,000.
🔄 Return of purchased shares.
📈 Another $700,000 if a stock-price condition was met.

It contains mutual releases for defined loan-sale & stock-purchase disputes.

📣 “The releases contained herein are not general releases…”

⚠️ No release in the tolling agreement does NOT mean McCabe never received one. These are TWO AGREEMENTS. The older release’s effect on potential trustee claims remains unresolved.

Hartman reports $7.2M total cash paid across the note purchase, stock purchases & settlement.

📣⚖️ COMPETING OFFERS

The trustee says Traudt’s April offer concerned different claims:

📣 “If Traudt or anyone else has a better bid for these two claims, the time to make it is now.”

🔎 His September objection also offers $100,000 + 50% of defined net recoveries for the SAME claims. Doc. 3002 does not expressly compare those terms. Funding, conditions & ability to perform still matter.

🏦✅ SAFEGUARDS

The trustee says payment precedes file transfer & counsel substitution, and settlements return for court approval.

Objectors question whether protections are clearly written into the agreement. The final agreement & order matter.

📅🏛️ NEXT

OCT. 13 — 1:30 PM Pacific / 4:30 PM Eastern. Judge Spraker may approve, require changes or more evidence, defer, or deny the sale.

A Washington state man allegedly helped plan a Canadian school massacre that killed eight people — including five students and an 11-year-old — then stayed awake after an overnight work shift to make sure the attack could be livestreamed for maximum attention.

James Cody Bryant, 30, was arrested Tuesday in Bellingham on a federal charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Prosecutors say Bryant sent money, offered advice and agreed to broadcast the Feb. 10 attack at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia. He and the 18-year-old shooter met through a random Omegle pairing roughly three years before the massacre and spent at least six months discussing violence.

FBI officials say Bryant admitted he may have been the only person who could have stopped the shooter — but chose to help instead. The livestream on Twitch lasted about 20 seconds before shutting down. Investigators say they do not know whether the shooter would have carried out the attack without Bryant's willingness to operate it.

Transgender Washington State resident accused of fueling deadly Canadian school massacre that killed 8: DOJ

Oct. 6, 2026

A transgender Washington State resident allegedly helped fuel a Canadian school massacre that left children dead, choosing to aid the shooter, who also identified as a transgender, instead of sounding the alarm, federal officials said Tuesday.

James Cody Bryant, 30, was arrested Tuesday morning in Bellingham north of Seattle, accused of sending money, offering advice and agreeing to broadcast the Feb. 10 attack at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia.

"Bryant had the information and ability to alert law enforcement, and even discussed that possibility with the shooter, but he chose not to," Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd said at a Seattle news conference.

"Instead, he encouraged and offered assistance to a murderer."

TRANSGEDNER EX-STUDENT IDENTIFIED AS ALLEGED SUSPECT IN CANADA SCHOOL MASS SHOOTING

U.S. and Canadian law enforcement officials announce an arrest connected to the Tumbler Ridge school shooting at a Seattle news conference

U.S. and Canadian officials discuss the arrest of James Cody Bryant, 30, in connection with the deadly Tumbler Ridge school shooting during a news conference Tuesday in Seattle. 

Bryant faces a federal charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country. Prosecutors allege Bryant helped the shooter, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, start a car to reach the school after the killings had begun.

"So even after the shooter had already tragically killed two family members, Bryant assisted the shooter in successfully traveling to the second location to take even more lives," FBI Seattle Special Agent in Charge W. Mike Herrington said.

"In the complaint, Bryant even admits to being maybe the only one who could stop the shooter."

Herrington confirmed that Bryant and Van Rootselaar both identified as transgender, and said Bryant identifies as female.

The two met through a random pairing on the online chat service Omegle roughly three years before the attack. 

Investigators have no indication what their transgender identities were, why they remained in contact, or that they ever met in person, Herrington said.

TEEN PLANNED MIDDLE SCHOOL MASSACRE BEFORE MAKING DEADLY ‘LAST-MINUTE CHOICE’ TO KILL MOM: OFFICIAL

Police tape surrounds the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and other buildings in Tumbler Ridge, Vancouver, British Columbia, Feb. 11, the day after a mass shooting there. (Jesse Boily /The Canadian Press via AP, File)

Their online friendship developed into discussions of violence over at least six months, according to Herrington.

"This complaint was particularly difficult to read, in part because of the casual tone these two individuals used when discussing the mass taking of innocent lives that was being planned," he said.

Bryant allegedly agreed to record and broadcast a livestream to maximize the shooter’s notoriety.

"Bryant even stayed awake after an overnight work shift to make sure this horrific act could be widely viewed online," Herrington said.

Police officers and investigators work outside Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, where a mass shooting took place in the small town of Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, Canada, on Feb. 10. 

"We certainly know the shooter was concerned that not enough people would see the livestream without Bryant broadcasting it, and was depending on Bryant to amplify the livestream because the shooter did not have many followers on social media."

Floyd said the attempted livestream on Twitch lasted about 20 seconds before shutting down.

🛎️ THE CLOSING BELL: TODAY'S FULL MARKET RECAP

Here's what you need to know:

🚨 #1. The S&P 500 closed at a fresh all-time high Tuesday, gaining 0.58%, while the Nasdaq added 0.45% for another record close and the Dow gained 0.49%. The biggest change versus Monday was some relief from the bond market, with the 10-year Treasury yield retreating toward 5.28% from multidecade highs, while continued AI strength helped equities push through record territory.

🚨 #2. Oil completely erased its early losses, with Brent ultimately settling UP 0.3% at $100.58 and WTI finishing essentially flat at $89.44. Rising Middle East exports and the planned G7 emergency-reserve release initially pressured crude, but geopolitical risk and extremely depleted inventories brought buyers back before settlement. Saudi Aramco warned today that more than 1 billion barrels have already been pulled from commercial inventories during the crisis and that much of the remaining global stockpile is not practically accessible.

#3. The U.S. trade deficit unexpectedly widened 13.7% in August to $105.6 billion, above the roughly $102 billion expected and the largest deficit in 17 months. Imports surged to an all-time record $420.8 billion despite the Trump administration's tariff push, driven partly by capital equipment, industrial supplies and technology needed for the AI infrastructure buildout. Economists estimate trade could subtract as much as 2.5 percentage points from Q3 GDP growth.

#4. Alphabet $GOOGL signed an enormous 3,590-megawatt power agreement with Constellation Energy $CEG as hyperscalers increasingly secure electricity directly for AI expansion. Constellation Energy $CEG will invest more than $4.3 billion, including upgrades to 11 nuclear units that will add 890 MW of new nuclear capacity, while another 2,700 MW will be supplied through the PJM grid. Constellation Energy $CEG surged roughly 12% on the news.

#5. Vice President JD Vance said Iran must substantially reduce its uranium-enrichment capacity for the war to end and the Strait of Hormuz to fully reopen. President Trump later added that his "biggest problem" is uncertainty over who actually controls Iran, saying the U.S. is unsure who has ultimate decision-making authority after the destruction of much of Iran's previous leadership. That uncertainty remains a major obstacle to reaching an enforceable agreement even as Gulf oil exports recover.

#6. The Middle East gained another energy-security risk as Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi airports in Jazan and Najran while fighting continued around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces are attempting to consolidate territory retaken near the shipping lane, while the Houthis have responded with missiles and drones against Saudi targets. Bab el-Mandeb has become even more important because Gulf producers are relying more heavily on alternative export routes while Hormuz remains disrupted.

#7. The Treasury sold $58 billion of three-year notes at a 4.932% yield, the highest auction yield for the maturity since May 2006. The bid-to-cover ratio came in at 2.62 versus a recent average around 2.65, while indirect bidder participation weakened, keeping Treasury demand under scrutiny ahead of Wednesday's $39 billion 10-year auction and Thursday's $22 billion 30-year sale.

#8. Marvell Technology $MRVL jumped nearly 6% after dramatically increasing its long-term AI growth expectations. Marvell $MRVL now expects roughly $20 billion of fiscal 2028 revenue and an extraordinary $70-$90 billion by fiscal 2031, versus current Wall Street estimates below $47 billion, while custom-chip revenue alone is expected to reach $12 billion in fiscal 2029. Broadcom $AVGO also rallied as investors continued pricing hyperscalers' shift toward internally designed AI accelerators alongside Nvidia $NVDA GPUs.

#9. Seagate $STX fell roughly 10% and Western Digital $WDC nearly 8% after a new development intensified concerns around the AI hard-drive market. Seagate $STX and Toshiba are reportedly competing to acquire TDK $TTDKY's magnetic-head business in a potentially multibillion-dollar deal; TDK $TTDKY is the only independent supplier of the critical HDD component. The battle adds another layer to the Toshiba capacity concerns that have already pressured both storage names.

#10. Becton Dickinson $BDX became the first major U.S. medical-device company to reach a tariff-relief agreement with the Trump administration, pledging $19 billion of U.S. investment over several years. The agreement protects qualifying Becton Dickinson $BDX products and inputs from future Section 232 tariffs if investment milestones are met, potentially establishing a template for similar deals across the medical-device industry.

#11. Option Care Health $OPCH surged roughly 33% after McKesson $MCK and Clayton Dubilier & Rice agreed to acquire the company in a transaction worth approximately $5.8 billion including debt. The $32.05-per-share offer represents a 37% premium to Monday's close, with CD&R taking roughly 51% ownership and McKesson $MCK investing about $1.4 billion for the remaining 49%.

#12. Penguin Solutions $PENG jumped again after hours after reporting a major beat-and-raise quarter driven by AI infrastructure demand. Revenue surged 68% YoY to a record $567 million versus roughly $521 million expected, adjusted EPS reached $1.00 versus $0.77 expected, and AI-driven businesses grew 141%. Penguin Solutions $PENG also raised its FY27 outlook to roughly $2.43 billion of revenue and $4.45 of EPS as its Advanced Computing business accelerates.

#13. Uber $UBER agreed to acquire workplace-catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in cash, expanding Uber Eats deeper into higher-value corporate food orders. ezCater generated more than $2.5 billion of gross bookings over the past year and connects businesses with more than 140,000 restaurants, giving Uber $UBER another route into enterprise spending through Uber for Business.

#14. Nvidia $NVDA-backed cloud provider Lambda is reportedly raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation in what could be its final private round before a 2027 IPO. Blackstone $BX and Coatue are reportedly leading the financing, while Lambda's unfilled-order backlog reportedly surged from $15 billion in June to roughly $50 billion by September as demand for AI compute continues outstripping available capacity.

That's your full market recap for October 6th, 2026 ✅

Subhashgram’s 
Half Kali, Half Durga: Ghoshbari’s 162-Year-Old Puja
In South 24 Parganas, this goddess is not like the Durga of any other house—she is half Kali and half Durga in the same body.
This puja, which began in 1864 under the hands of Harikishore Ghosh, still retains that unique character even today.
It is said that while working as a daroga (police officer) in Medinimandal of Dhaka, Harikishore received a divine command from the goddess in a dream. When the artisans first started colouring the idol yellow, the right side of the image suddenly turned black. Harikishore remembered the dream. On the advice of the priest, the goddess was installed in that very form.

Even after the family moved to Subhashgram following the Partition, the rituals of the puja did not change.
The single-structure (ekchala) idol has its right side black and left side golden. The right foot rests on the lion’s back, the left foot on the asura’s shoulder. On the goddess’s right stand Lakshmi and Kartik; on the left stand Saraswati and Ganesha—quite different from the usual arrangement.
Following the rules of the Brihannandikeshwar Purana, 108 kinds of water are used for the bathing ritual on Saptami. Pumpkin and sugarcane sacrifices continue for all three days.
 The most unusual, however, is the ‘Shatru-bali’ (enemy sacrifice) on Navami—an effigy of a human is made from powdered rice and then sacrificed, symbolising the suppression of evil tendencies in the human mind.
In this household, cooked rice is never offered as naivedya. Instead, 12.5 kg of raw rice is given. The bhog on Dashami includes homemade items such as kochu lati (taro stem), shapla-shaluk (water lilies), amra (hog plum), and boro dhan rice.
This is an unique puja culture 🙏

text:
Cyrus Ingerson Scofield (1843–1921) was a Confederate veteran, Kansas lawyer, and politician who served as U.S. Attorney for Kansas until he resigned in 1876 amid corruption charges. He was dogged by accusations of forgery, bribery, land fraud, and embezzlement. He abandoned his first wife and children, remarried, and later reinvented himself as a Congregational minister.
In 1909 he published the Scofield Reference Bible, whose footnotes imported Darby's dispensationalism and the pre-tribulation rapture into mainstream American evangelicalism. He was no Hebrew or Greek scholar; the notes were largely borrowed and stitched together to serve a theology that severed the Church from Israel's covenants and turned the Gospel into an escapist scheme.
In short: a shady operator whose personal life and financial ethics were a wreck, and whose Bible notes did enormous damage to American Christianity by popularizing the rapture lie.

The transition from the Mosaic age to the New Covenant is the central narrative of the New Testament. The following passages confirm that the promises once held by the nation of Israel now reside solely in the Church, the body of Christ.
The True Israel and the New Covenant
After the Parable of the Vineyard, Jesus declares to the Jewish leadership: "Therefore I say to you, the kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and given to a nation producing the fruit of it." This is a explicit termination of the covenantal status of the old ethnos and its transfer to the Church, which is the "holy nation" (1 Peter 2:9).Matthew 21:43 – The Transfer of the Kingdom
The author of Hebrews makes the transition absolute: "In that He says, ‘A new covenant,’ He has made the first old. Now what is becoming obsolete and growing old is ready to vanish away." This was written prior to 70 AD, pointing toward the imminent, total destruction of the Temple and the legalistic system that the author correctly identified as a fading relic.Hebrews 8:13 – The Obsolescence of the Old
Paul dismantles ethnic privilege in the covenant: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise." Covenant membership is defined by union with Christ, not biological descent. Those who reject Christ have no claim to the promises made to Abraham.Galatians 3:28–29 – The Definition of the Seed
Paul clarifies that ethnicity is irrelevant to election: "For they are not all Israel who are of Israel, nor are they all children because they are the seed of Abraham... That is, those who are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God; but the children of the promise are counted as the seed." This destroys the notion of a "chosen" group outside of the faith.Romans 9:6–8 – Lineage Does Not Equal Promise
In the letters to the churches of Smyrna and Philadelphia, Christ identifies those who claim the title of "Jew" but reject Him as a "synagogue of Satan." This is not a reference to a future end-times group, but an immediate indictment of the religious leaders and followers of the old system who actively persecuted the early Church. It serves as a stark reminder that rejection of the Messiah places one in opposition to God, regardless of ancestral claims.Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 – The Synagogue of Satan
Peter applies the language of the Exodus and the Old Covenant directly to the Church: "But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people... who once were not a people but are now the people of God." The title of "God's chosen people" is now the permanent possession of the Church, having been stripped from the covenant-breakers of the old age.1 Peter 2:9–10 – The New Identity
The historic Church understood that Christ is the fulfillment of all prophecy. By replacing the Temple with His own body and the national covenant with the Church, He ended the era of tribal legalism and ushered in the era of His own universal, spiritual kingdom.

The heresy of rebuilding a physical temple in Jerusalem is the rejection of the finished work of Jesus Christ. It is a direct assault on the New Covenant. Here is the breakdown:
The Bible explicitly teaches that Christ offered Himself as the one, perfect, and final sacrifice for all time (Hebrews 10:12). To attempt to reinstitute animal sacrifices is to claim that Christ’s blood was insufficient and that the old, fading order is superior to the New Covenant. It is a return to "beggarly elements" that God abolished.1. It denies the sufficiency of the Cross
The Old Testament temple was merely a shadow (a type) pointing toward the true Temple. Christ said, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up," referring to His own body (John 2:19-21). Now, the Church—the body of believers—is the Temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 3:16). Building a structure of stone today is an act of idolatry that ignores that God now dwells in His people, not in a building made by hands.2. It confuses the Temple's identity
Modern Zionism and Christian Zionism promote the idea that the Jewish people retain a separate, valid covenant status apart from Christ. This is false. The modern Jewish movement to rebuild the Temple explicitly seeks to restore the Levitical priesthood and animal sacrifice, which are diametrically opposed to the Gospel. Supporting this, even from a "prophetic" standpoint, is effectively participating in the denial of Christ’s Messiahship.3. It is "Judaizing" (Christ-denying)
The destruction of the Temple in 70 AD was God’s final, physical "seal" on the end of the Mosaic age. By attempting to rebuild what God Himself destroyed and declared obsolete (Hebrews 8:13), advocates are attempting to resurrect a dead system of works and blood-sacrifice that Christ replaced with His own once-for-all atonement.4. It is a rejection of Preterist fulfillment
In short, it is blasphemous. It treats the Gospel as a temporary stopgap rather than the ultimate, eternal fulfillment of God’s plan.

text:
It is real there is practical difference in temple rituals between North and South on who performs aarti/abhishek but not absolute.

South (major Agama temples): core rituals usually limited to trained archakas under Shaiva Agamas, Vaikhanasa or Pancharatra or many village temples by traditional pujari caste archakas by hereditary. Devotees receive the deepa or prasadam while direct performance and garbhagriha access stay restricted. Courts have upheld these Agama rules.

North: more variable and participatory. Formal aartis at big temples (e.g. Kashi Vishwanath) are still priest-led, but closer access and limited devotee involvement are common elsewhere when not crowded.

Why the gap: Grihyasutras (Paraskara, Gobhila in the North) the domestic manuals for rutuals — the householder himself offers deepa, water or flowers at home. They do not authorize lay aarti inside a temple. Agamas later absorbed some Grihya procedures but added strict rules on who may serve a consecrated murti. The South kept those Agama priesthoods intact. In much of the North, temple institutions and ritual lineages were repeatedly broken by mleccha invasions after the late 12th century, so later revivals by local community drew more on Puranic and householder (grihya-style) models. That produced wider overlap between home worship and temple practice.

Regional styles already differed earlier; political disruption amplified the contrast. I am not sure how RJB temple followed before modi built this modern mostly non agamic structure over RJB - in any case Modern VIP aarti is administrative access to agamic murtis in  North, not scriptural right, in south VIPs get much closer access to murti but aarti is still performed by the proest.

I can be wrong in my assessment / some of the historical inferences.

text:
The Most Holy Rosary
October 7th

“On the same day, in the Roman martyrology, the commemoration of our Lady of Victory, established under the circumstances mentioned on the first Sunday of this month. Although the Virgin of virgins gave to the youthful martyr Justina a share in the triumph of Lepanto, nevertheless the chief honor of the day redounds to Mary herself. It behooves us, then, to renew our homage to the Queen of the holy rosary, on the exact anniversary of her deliverance of Christendom under that title. Let us do so by offering her the three hymns of her Office, which recall the joyful, sorrowful, and glorious mysteries of the rosary, and which are epitomized in that of second Vespers given on the feast. (The four hymns are of the eighteenth century. Though now slightly modified, the three here given were composed by Thomas Ricchini, Master of the second d’alace, and that of second Vespers by the Dominican Eustace Sirena.)” 

HYMN OF FIRST VESPERS

The messenger of the heavenly court, disclosing the hidden mysteries of the Divinity, hails as full of grace the Virgin about to become Mother of God.

The Virgin visits her relative, the mother of John, who, though yet a captive in the womb, leaps with joy announcing the presence of Christ.

The Word that before all ages had proceeded from the Father’s Intellect, is born a mortal Babe of a Virgin Mother.

The little One is presented in the temple, the Legislator obeys the Law, the Redeemer offers himself in sacrifice, and is redeemed at a pauper’s price.

And now the joyful Mother finds her Son, whom she had mourned as lost; finds him expounding to learned minds things unknown to them.

Glory be to thee, O Jesus born of the Virgin; together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, through everlasting ages. Amen.

HYMN OF MATINS

On the mount with olives planted, prostrate the Redeemer prays; he grieves, he fears, he well-nigh faints, pouring forth a sweat of blood.

God, delivered up by a traitor, is dragged away to punishment; bound with tight bonds, he bleeds beneath the cruel scourges.

A crown of ignominy, woven of sharp thorns, adorns the King of glory clothed with purple tatters.

Laboring, breathless, thrice falling beneath the heavy cross, he his compelled by force to bear it to the mountain-top.

Nailed to the awful gibbet, the Innocent hangs between two criminals; till, praying for his torturers, he yields up his Spirit with the last drop of his Blood.

Glory be to thee, O Jesus born of the Virgin; together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, through everlasting ages. Amen.

HYMN OF LAUDS

Death overthrown, Christ rises victorious from limbo, and breaking the bonds of sin, throws open heaven’s gate.

Having appeared long enough to men, he ascends to the heavenly dwellings, and is enthroned at his Father’s right hand, a partner in his glory.

The Holy Spirit, whom he had promised to give them, he sends down upon his sorrowing disciples in fiery tongues of love.

With her body set free from earthly weight, the Virgin is raised above the stars; she is welcomed with heaven’s jubilant delight, and with the songs of angels.

Twelve stars now crown the lovely Mother’s brow; and from her throne beside her Son, she reigns over all creation.

Glory be to thee, O Jesus born of the Virgin; together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, through everlasting ages. Amen.

(The Liturgical Year, 1841-1875, Dom Prosper Guéranger)

The N-T-S-B has released its preliminary report on the deadly news helicopter crash outside Los Angeles.
NewsNation's BLAKE BURMAN reports: “The agency finding that the helicopter flew around the scene of a bus crash for 1 hour and 24 minutes. Video from the scene shows the helicopter was operating normally until the last 30 seconds. The recording captured advisories related to the helicopter's main rotor. The crash left the crew on board and a man on the ground dead. They'd been covering a bus crash below.
Officials have since identified them as reporter Eliana Moreno, pilot George Marciniw and pedestrian Edy Gutierrez Mejia.

Tropical Depression Nine has formed in the Gulf, expected to strengthen into the Atlantic's first hurricane of the season.. NewsNation Meteorologist Chris Franklin says the National Hurricane Center thinks it could strengthen into a category two storm before it potentially makes landfall later this week: “What we know right now is the rain probably doesn't start until early Friday morning, most of the day Friday and into the start of the day Saturday. So expect more changes and stay tuned. And what I'm gonna be watching is what is the strength and structure of the storm by Thursday. That is when the hurricane center is expecting that northerly motion. ”

Cartels Plot to Kidnap Border Agents in Texas

An internal Department of Homeland Security alert warns that a known alien smuggler linked to the cartels is preparing to move groups of illegal immigrants from Colombia and Venezuela across the Texas border with the explicit aim of targeting and kidnapping Customs and Border Protection personnel. The threat focuses on the Presidio and El Paso sectors.

The alert, obtained by NewsNation correspondent Ali Bradley, states that the operation’s purpose may include attempts to seize federal agents and officers. It arrives days after suspected cartel gunmen fired on a U.S. Coast Guard vessel along the Rio Grande, prompting the deployment of roughly 500 troops by helicopter into the Rio Grande Valley.

CBP responded that it maintains proactive intelligence on foreign threats, vets reports with partners, and uses robust but undisclosed methods to protect its people. The agency declined to detail those measures.

The warning fits a documented pattern of cartel bounties and direct attacks on federal officers after tighter border enforcement cut into smuggling revenue. Agents in the region have already faced shootings and explicit offers of payment for assaults and kidnappings.
